question.problem: The function $f(x)=4\operatorname{ln}⁡(kx-3)+1$ has an inverse function given by ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{3}\cdot {e}^{(x-1)/4}+1.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡(kx-3)+1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡(ky-3)+1.\end{aligned}
$$

We make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡(ky-3)+1 \\ 4\operatorname{ln}⁡(ky-3) & =x-1 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(ky-3) & =\frac{x-1}{4} \\ {e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(ky-3)} & ={e}^{(x-1)/4} \\ ky-3 & ={e}^{(x-1)/4} \\ ky & ={e}^{(x-1)/4}+3 \\ y & =\frac{1}{k}({e}^{(x-1)/4}+3) \\ y & =\frac{1}{k}\cdot {e}^{(x-1)/4}+\frac{3}{k}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{k}\cdot {e}^{(x-1)/4}+\frac{3}{k}.$ 

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=3.$
